osrec_user_memory_object.reason: OSREC runtime lookup of an admitted caller object in the replay's user-memory map; user bytes are not kernel entry state
osrec_user_memory_object.implementation: include/osrec/syscall_slice.h user-memory contract, populated from the SVC boundary's admitted user objects

state_ranges.reason: the slice fdtable holds 64 inline descriptor slots and bitmap words for 64 descriptors

input_domains.reason: a regular-file position is never negative: vfs_llseek and rw_verify_area reject negative offsets without FMODE_UNSIGNED_OFFSET, which ramfs and memfd files do not set
each file reference is held by a descriptor slot, mapping or task, so the count stays far below LONG_MAX and get_file cannot overflow
expand_fdtable sets resize_in_progress and clears it before returning within one call; with the files table not shared (a single-threaded task), no resize is in progress at a system-call boundary

klee_separate_members.reason: file reads and writes index file_data.bytes at f_pos + i; in its own KLEE object those symbolic-index accesses stay out of the rest of the context

graph_invariants.reason: between system calls of a single-threaded task no descriptor is reserved without being installed: alloc_fd sets the bit and fd_install fills the slot within one call, and close clears both, so open_fds equals the installed slots
full_fds_bits records which open_fds words are all ones (__set_open_fd and __clear_open_fd keep it in step)
next_fd is a search hint never above the lowest free descriptor: alloc_fd advances it past the allocated slot and __put_unused_fd/close lower it to the freed one
